findings.title: New internal test file omits the established testpackage nolint directive
findings.detail: archive_internal_test.go is `package cli` — an internal test, as its own top comment says ("like slug_test.go") — but every other internal (package cli) test file in this package carries `//nolint:testpackage // tests an unexported helper` immediately above the package clause: internal/cli/slug_test.go:1, internal/cli/revision_test.go:1, internal/cli/brief_stable_test.go, internal/cli/cmd_review_test.go, internal/cli/cmd_review_cache_test.go, internal/cli/cmd_record_test.go, and internal/bundle/state_test.go/write_test.go. .golangci.yml enables the `testpackage` linter and only exempts `_test\.go` files from bodyclose/dupl/errcheck/funlen/goconst/gosec/noctx/wrapcheck (line 463-472) — testpackage is not in that exempt list. Without the directive, `golangci-lint run` will flag this new file exactly where every sibling internal test file in the package is consistently suppressed.

findings.title: New Grace/verifyMargin constants duplicate cmd_review.go/cmd_verify.go's existing ones, un-unified for now
findings.detail: deadline.go:72 adds `Grace = 30 * time.Second` — task 2's own brief describes this as "cmd_review.go's reviewGrace moves here (value unchanged)" — and deadline.go:76 adds an unexported `verifyMargin = 30 * time.Second`. Neither call site is repointed at the new package in this wave: internal/cli/cmd_review.go:82 still declares its own `reviewGrace = 30 * time.Second` (used at cmd_review.go:176), internal/cli/cmd_verify.go:15 still declares its own `verifyMargin = 30 * time.Second` (used at cmd_verify.go:111), and internal/cli/cmd_close_wave.go:30's fixed `closeWaveTimeout = 30 * time.Minute` is untouched even though deadline_test.go's own worked example (TestCloseBudgetsTheWave, 'eight tasks... exceeds today's fixed 30m') proves a realistic 8-task wave already needs 192m. This is evidently staged for a later task (the plan's alignment-verdicts.md describes call-site rewiring as a separate step), so it is not this wave's own tasks failing to do their job, but it does leave two independent, untested-for-drift 30s constants (and a stale 30m cap) coexisting in the tree in the meantime — unlike task 1's defaultTimeout/defaultBackendTimeout pair, which does get an explicit equality test (internal/cli/backend_timeout_test.go).
